arxiv-2203-01605.description: Abstract The Advanced Wakefield (AWAKE) Experiment is a proof-of-principle experiment demonstrating the acceleration of electron beams via proton-driven plasma wakefield acceleration. AWAKE Run 1 achieved acceleration of electron beams to 2 GeV 2\text{\,}\mathrm{GeV} and the intention for Run 2 is to build on these results by achieving acceleration to ∼ \sim 10 GeV 10\text{\,}\mathrm{GeV} with a higher beam quality.

A 2023 arXiv research paper by Bohan Lu, Christian Bertoni, Steven J. Thomson, Jens Eisert. I
Abstract

Quasi-local integrals of motion are a key concept underpinning the modern understanding of many-body localisation, an intriguing phenomenon in which interactions and disorder come together.

arxiv-2304-13235.title: Anyon Quantum Dimensions from an Arbitrary Ground State Wave Function
arxiv-2304-13235.creator: Shang Liu
arxiv-2304-13235.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shang Liu. Realizing topological orders and topological quantum computation is a central task of modern physics. An important but notoriously hard question in this endeavor is how to diagnose topological orders that lack conventional order parameters. A breakthrough in this problem is the discovery of topological entanglement entropy, which can be used to detect nontrivial topological order from a ground state wave function, but is far from enough for fully determining the topological order.

arxiv-2505-23147.description: Abstract . Advances in eye-tracking control for assistive robotic arms provide intuitive interaction opportunities for people with physical disabilities. Shared control has gained interest in recent years by improving user satisfaction through partial automation of robot control. We present an eye-tracking-guided shared control design based on insights from state-of-the-art literature.

pmc-10672613.title: Is the Direct Fixation of Displaced Quadrilateral Plates in Acetabular Fractures Necessary?
pmc-10672613.creator: Beom-Soo Kim, Ki-Cheor Bae, Chul-Hyun Cho, Kyung-Jae Lee, In Gyu Lee, Min-Gyu Lee, Byung-Woo Min
pmc-10672613.description: Quadrilateral plate fractures represent a heterogeneous group of acetabular fractures. Accurate reduction is required to prevent post-traumatic arthritis. The purpose of this study is to determine the reduction effect of the direct fixation of quadrilateral plates in acetabular fractures, and to evaluate the strength of direct fixation compared to indirect fixation.

pmc-10718319.title: Identification of a valuable gene network for the diagnosis and treatment of non-obstructive azoospermia: in-silico analyses – experimental research
pmc-10718319.creator: Mohammad Reza Zabihi, Narges Norouzkhani, Samad Karkhah, Mohammad Akhoondian
pmc-10718319.description: Introduction:Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is an etiology of infertility in men. NOA may have various classifications; however, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism can be regarded as a class of NOA associated with genetic factors. Former studies have shown that noncoding RNA (ncRNA) plays an essential role in NOA incidence, but few studies have been performed on the NOA-related ncRNA interaction network.

pmc-10759631.title: Dealer-customer partnership in rice production demonstration: Assessment of private extension system in Bangladesh
pmc-10759631.creator: Tanjina Parven, Md Safiul Islam Afrad, Shaikh Shamim Hasan, Sajia Sharmin, Muhammad Ashraful Habib, Swati Nayak, Saidul Islam, Aliyu Akilu Barau, Amlan Biswas, Md Shibly Sadik
pmc-10759631.description: Traditional public extension worker-farmer cooperation in rice production demonstration is not working efficiently, therefore, private partnership-based demonstration has been attempted to introduce as its alternative very recently involving dealer-customer farmer. The study evaluated the private extension services rendered through dealer-customer farmer cooperation in Bangladesh. Thirty-three rice seed dealers and ninety-two customer farmers formed the samples for the study.

pmc-11313456.title: Integrated Use of Furnace Bottom Ash as Fine Aggregate and Cement Replacement for Sustainable Mortar Production
pmc-11313456.creator: Waiching Tang, Ali M Onaizi, Sagheer A Onaizi, Umer Sajjad, Yanju Liu, Dolores Eliche Quesada
pmc-11313456.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Recycling fly ash (FA) and furnace bottom ash (FBA) help with reducing greenhouse gas emissions, conserving natural resources, and minimizing waste accumulation. However, research on recycling FBA is progressing more slowly compared to FA. This research aims to investigate the combined use of FBA as a replacement for both fine aggregate and cement and its influence on the performance of mortar.

pmc-11579425.title: Deciphering molecular landscape of breast cancer progression and insights from functional genomics and therapeutic explorations followed by in vitro validation
pmc-11579425.creator: Bushra Khan, Rowaid Qahwaji, Mashael S. Alfaifi, Tanwir Athar, Abdullah Khan, Mohammad Mobashir, Ibraheem Ashankyty, Khalid Imtiyaz, Areej Alahmadi, M. Moshahid A. Rizvi
pmc-11579425.description: Breast cancer is caused by aberrant breast cells that proliferate and develop into tumors. Tumors have the potential to spread throughout the body and become lethal if ignored. Metastasis is the process by which invasive tumors move to neighboring lymph nodes or other organs. Metastasis can be lethal and perhaps fatal.

pmc-12452840.title: An examination of anhedonia as a predictor of response with transcranial magnetic stimulation treatment for youth with depression☆
pmc-12452840.creator: Jacquelin C Hecker, Paul A Nakonezny, Cicek N Bakir, Irem Azamet, Magdalena Romanowicz, Julia Shekunov, Jennifer L Vande Voort, J Luis Lujan, Paul E Croarkin
pmc-12452840.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This exploratory study examined the relationship between the change in anhedonia symptoms and treatment response in adolescents receiving 1 Hz or 10 Hz transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD).

pmc-12586235.title: Patient expectations and concerns regarding robotic thyroidectomy in china: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12586235.creator: Ling Zhan, Siyi Zhu, Zheng Ding, Bomin Guo, Xianzhao Deng, Bo Wu, Zhili Yang, Minggao Guo, Youben Fan
pmc-12586235.description: Robotic thyroidectomy (RT) has gained increasing patient interest and clinical adoption in China. However, patient perceptions of RT remain poorly understood. A cross-sectional survey of 211 patients who had previously heard of RT was conducted to explore their attitudes, expectations and concerns regarding the procedure. Of the participants, 158 (74.9%) were female, with a median age of 36.

pmc-13470632.title: Reactivation after total thyroidectomy? A thyroid eye disease case that challenges established clinical paradigms
pmc-13470632.creator: Alejandra Niño Alarcón, Diana Cristina Henao, Leonardo Rojas, Ana María Gomez, Yeimer Ortiz Martínez
pmc-13470632.description: SummaryThyroid eye disease (TED) is the most common extrathyroidal manifestation of Graves’ disease, with an incidence of approximately 1.9 cases per 10,000 inhabitants per year. Its pathophysiology involves an autoimmune response mediated by TSH receptor antibodies (TRAbs), leading to inflammation, fibroblast activation, and orbital tissue remodeling. Although TED typically becomes inactive within 1–3 years, 5–10% of patients experience recurrences.
